# A rail reveal paints the browser's focus ring around the whole overlay

## Context

The 13.2 notes frame D2 (`dock-d2-rail.png` in neomjs/pages `resources_pub/website/release-notes/v13.2.0/`) shows a light-blue ring around the System Metrics overlay, which is revealed from the right edge rail. The operator (2026-10-10) saw no ring in the film takes or when using the rail by hand. Sampled pixels of the frame show the ring is `#99C8FF` with a `#101010` edge. That is Chrome's default dark-scheme focus ring, not the overlay's designed border (`--dock-reveal-border`: `--workstation-signal` at 46% over `--workstation-line`, a teal-grey).

## The Problem

Whether the ring paints depends on what held focus before the reveal, not on the reveal itself. A real mouse click never paints it: Chrome's last-input heuristic says pointer. The film driver's rail step (`apps/workstation/tour/GestureDriver.mjs:673-704`, #19127) clicks with synthetic events (`detail` 0) and then calls `button.focus()` with no modality. That programmatic focus is focus-visible, and the overlay's programmatic focus inherits it. The frame is embedded in the 13.2 notes, and every scripted capture of a reveal can repeat it.

## The Architectural Reality

- `Rail#onRevealStateChange` (`src/dashboard/dock/interaction/Rail.mjs:740-741`) calls `RevealOverlay#focusReveal()` when a tab click opens a reveal (`revealed-focused`). `Rail#onTabClick` (`:777`) receives the click payload, which carries `detail` (`src/main/DomEvents.mjs:329`). `detail` is ≥ 1 for a pointer click and 0 for a keyboard- or AT-activated one.
- `focusReveal()` (`src/dashboard/dock/interaction/RevealOverlay.mjs:390-396`) calls `this.focus(this.id, true)` with no modality. The root is `tabIndex: -1`. `DomUtils.isFocusable` (`src/main/DomUtils.mjs:128-131`) accepts a negative tab index, so the root itself takes focus.
- `DomAccess#focus` (`src/main/DomAccess.mjs:358-400`) stamps `neo-focus-pointer` for `'pointer'` and says it "suppresses the accidental ring", but no stylesheet keys on that class. Only the Grid view styles its own focus (#18968, `resources/scss/src/grid/View.scss:9-19`). The contract is unbacked for all three callers that state `'pointer'`: `RevealOverlay.mjs:538`, `src/draggable/container/SortZone.mjs:681` and `src/grid/Body.mjs:1277`.
- Deliberate outlines share the property: the locked pane (`resources/scss/src/dashboard/Container.scss:916`) and the arrival pulse (`:372`). A suppression rule must lose to every author rule and beat only the user agent's.

Design authority: `DomAccess#focus` (`src/main/DomAccess.mjs:358-360`): *"explicit input-modality contract. :focus-visible cannot tie an async worker→main programmatic focus back to the originating pointer gesture, so the caller states it."* The same method's comment says *"'pointer' suppresses the accidental ring"*.

## The Fix

1. `resources/scss/src/Global.scss`: `:where(.neo-focus-pointer:focus-visible) {outline: none}`. With zero specificity it beats only the user-agent ring, and any component outline still wins. The `DomAccess#focus` comment names this rule.
2. `Rail#onTabClick` records the opening gesture's modality (`'pointer'` when `detail >= 1`), and `focusReveal(modality)` passes it to `focus()`. A keyboard-opened reveal passes none, so the user agent's keyboard ring stays.
3. The film driver's synthetic click carries `detail: 1`, as a real click does.
4. D2 is reshot at the fixed head, with the same path and caption, so the notes embed is unchanged.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC-1 Red first in a real browser: an e2e arm focuses the rail tab programmatically (the film driver's path), opens the reveal with a click of `detail: 1`, and asserts that the focused overlay root's computed `outline-style` is `none`. The arm is red on `dev`.
- [ ] AC-2 Green at the head. A keyboard-opened reveal (Enter on the tab) keeps a visible ring on the focused overlay root (control arm, green on both).
- [ ] AC-3 Deliberate outlines are unchanged: the DockLock component spec (`outline-style: solid` on a locked pane) and the dashboard e2e folder stay green.
- [ ] AC-4 *(Post-Merge)* D2 is reshot without the ring, and the pages `main` URL serves the new bytes.

## Out of Scope

Component keyboard rings keyed on `:focus-visible` instead of `neo-focus-keyboard`, and the look of the keyboard ring around the overlay root (it stays the user agent's).

### @neo-opus-grace - 2026-10-10T13:37:43Z

Intake (self-authored, stage 2). Prescription checked: `src/main/DomAccess.mjs`. A better owner than the overlay's own SCSS is `resources/scss/src/Global.scss`: DomAccess documents that `'pointer'` suppresses the accidental ring, but nothing consumes `neo-focus-pointer`. So the contract is unbacked for all three callers that state it, not only the reveal. A zero-specificity global rule backs it without erasing the deliberate outlines that share the property (the locked pane, the arrival pulse). A component opt-out would have removed the keyboard ring too. The body is updated (The Problem, Reality, Fix, ACs).
